news.title: Susan Collins Ditches JD Vance as He Campaigns for Her
news.description: Vice President JD Vance has made two trips to Maine to stump for Republican Senator Susan Collins as her midterm election against Democrat Troy Jackson approaches. Yet Collins has been a no-show for each visit, leading to speculation that she is deliberately avoiding the vice president and the greater Trump administration. In his latest visit to Maine on Monday, Vance heaped praise on Collins during a rally at defense technology manufacturer Compotech. “Whenever I’m in the great state of Maine ... I gotta give Susan a little bit of crap,” Vance said at the rally. “Susan is the most independent member of the United States Senate, and as the president of the United States Senate, she sometimes makes my job just a little bit harder. But she makes it harder because she is coming to work every single day and fighting not for a political party.... She fights for the great people of Maine.” Vance also mentioned that Collins had been to his house about six times. Vance: "The second shout out I gotta give is to my dear friend Susan Collins, the senator from Maine. Thank you!...She has been to my house probably a half dozen times, the Vice President's residence at the Naval Observatory." pic.twitter.com/JOipfRFFCA — BulwarkClips (@BulwarkClips) August 24, 2026 It’s no surprise Collins didn’t show up to the rally. President Trump has a nearly 60 percent disapproval rating among Mainers as of last month, and nothing indicates any future improvement. The vast majority of Mainers don’t think their state is affordable, and Maine business has suffered significantly due to the most recent 50 percent tariff trade war the Trump administration started with Canada. Collins has made a point to distance herself from Trump on his new tariffs threat against Canada, saying that they would be a “ mistake .” She also drew a line in the sand against the administration’s attack on mail-in ballots, which she called “ very important to the people of Maine,” particularly seniors. Collins was called out by Jackson the morning of the rally. “How ‘bout fuel prices going through the roof because of the war on Iran? How ‘bout ICE murdering people here in Biddeford? Let’s give a shoutout to Susan Collins about how poor of a job she’s doing for the state of Maine. I’m sure JD Vance loves her because she’s doing everything that he wants for her,” he said . “But she’s not doing it for Maine people.” My message to Susan's pal @JDVance who’s coming to Maine today pic.twitter.com/mOMz4QqHFc — Troy Jackson (@TroyJackson207) August 24, 2026

news.title: Susan Collins refuses to utter JD Vance's name as she snubs him at event
news.description: Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) refused to even say Vice President JD Vance's name as she announced she would not join his campaign stop in Maine on Monday. The move comes as Collins trails former Maine Senate president Troy Jackson, the Democratic nominee, in a race that could determine control of the U.S. Senate, according to recent polling. Vance spoke at Compotech, a defense contractor in Brewer, without her. At a weekend parade, a reporter put the question directly to Collins. "Monday, the vice president is visiting Brewer to go to Compotech," the reporter said. "I'm curious. Will we see you there, and what are your thoughts on the vice president coming to Maine?" In response, Collins never said Vance's name but referred to Energy Secretary Doug Wright twice. "I always welcome anyone coming to the state of Maine," Collins replied. "Just recently, I was with the secretary of Energy in Lincoln, Maine, where we celebrated this new battery technology that is cutting edge and will help the resilience of the electric grid in New England. I am already scheduled on Monday, so I will not be able to join the vice president. But I really appreciated Secretary Wright's presence." Collins campaign spokesperson Shawn Roderick confirmed Monday that Collins would not attend, saying she has a "great working relationship" with Vance but a "personal schedule" that would keep her away, the outlet reported. According to the Portland Press Herald , GOP gubernatorial nominee Bobby Charles is also skipping the event, though former Maine Gov. Paul LePage is expected to attend. American Bridge, a Democratic-aligned political action committee, argued Collins is dodging Vance in person while pointing to their prior dealings, the Bangor Daily News reported. Those dealings include a dinner with Vance before Collins voted to confirm Tulsi Gabbard as director of national intelligence. "Sometimes I get frustrated with Susan Collins," Vance said at a Bangor rally in May, adding that he almost wished she were "more partisan" — before endorsing her reelection bid. On Saturday, Collins also broke with the administration over its decision to impose 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, her office said , calling on both countries to return to negotiations. "The Administration must consider the negative impact tariffs would have on Maine businesses, communities, and families and work to reach a fair agreement with our Canadian neighbors," Collins wrote. The latest Fox News poll shows Jackson leading Collins 48% to 46%, within the margin of error, in a race that could determine Senate control.
